summary.summary: Brentwood's covering report presents the unaudited (pre-audit) Statement of Accounts 2025/26, certified by the s151 officer as true and fair and published by the 30 June statutory deadline, with the audited version due by 31 January 2027. The statutory public inspection period runs 1 July to 11 August 2026 and had drawn no requests to see documents and no representations to the external auditors at the time of writing. The accounts are prepared on a going-concern basis, resting on the council's reserves and its track record of delivering efficiencies, and the report explicitly states that looming local government reorganisation does not change that view because vesting is beyond the 12-month horizon. The financial statements themselves are Appendix A, a separate document, so this paper carries no balance-sheet figures.

news_drafts.headline: Brentwood's capital spending plan falls 25% behind in first quarter, creating delivery risk
news_drafts.lead: Brentwood council is on track to spend only three-quarters of its planned capital expenditure in the first quarter of 2026/27, with a £13.6 million shortfall against a £54.5 million budget. The underspend masks volatile performance across individual projects. The council's affordable housing programme, budgeted at £37.2 million for the quarter, is forecast to spend only £26.2 million, a 30 per cent slip. Meanwhile, the Baytree project is running at just 20 per cent of its planned £5 million spend. However, two other major projects are overrunning: the Depot Redevelopment faces a £1 million overspend and the Brentwood Centre Redevelopment a £591,000 overspend. The quarterly shortfall raises questions about whether the council can deliver its capital programme on schedule.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for Internal Audit Q2 Update 2026/27
findings.headline: Waste Management recommendation 1, first due June 2024, is closed after the Waste Improvement Plan was approved on 07/09/2026.
findings.detail: The Waste Improvement Plan covers an approximate two-year period and sets out the direction of travel for the service. Management says a longer-term strategy will be revisited separately from the audit recommendations. Internal audit closed the recommendation after receiving management confirmation and reviewing the plan.
findings.matters: The recommendation was revised three times before closure, and closure rests on a two-year plan rather than the longer-term strategy originally recommended, which matters to councils setting their own waste strategies.
findings.figures: Due dates June 2024, June 2025, June 2026 and September 2026; plan approved 07/09/2026
findings.quote: The Waste Improvement Plan was approved by

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for Internal Audit Q2 Update 2026/27
findings.headline: Revenues and Benefits Partnership recommendation 3, on documented procedures for contract changes and Partnership Board approval, is overdue with a revised date of December 2026.
findings.detail: Shared service and Partnership Board meetings are being documented and retained. The wider element, covering formal change procedures and documented approval of contract modifications, is not yet complete. Management says the work has been folded into a wider Revenues and Benefits service review that takes account of Local Government Reorganisation.
findings.matters: Change control and board approval of modifications to a shared service contract is a governance point for any council in a partnership, and the review's link to LGR affects the contract's future.
findings.figures: Original due date April 2026; revised dates September 2026 and December 2026
findings.quote: One recommendation for Revenues and Benefits Partnership remains as Overdue.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for Internal Audit Q2 Update 2026/27
findings.headline: Aids and Adaptations recommendation 3, on contractor pricing and payments, is closed, with Axis price book prices now stated as per the contract agreements.
findings.detail: Management reports that all Axis price book prices now match the contract agreements. A new process requires two quotes for works below £10k and three quotes for works above £10k, and a spreadsheet of approved works and costs is kept to check payments against the quotes. Internal audit closed the recommendation after reviewing that spreadsheet.
findings.matters: Payments to a contractor being checked against the schedule of works and the contract price book is a control a finance director would expect to see in any adaptations or similar contractor-paid service.
findings.figures: Two quotes below £10k; three quotes above £10k; due date September 2026; status Closed
findings.quote: The process states two quotes for anything below £10k

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for Internal Audit Q2 Update 2026/27
findings.headline: Trade Waste recommendation 3a, on the Corporate Sundry Debt Management, Recovery & Write-Off Policy, is closed after the Debt Management Policy was updated.
findings.detail: Management reports the policy has been updated and that checks are ongoing to ensure customers' accounts are being paid. Where issues arise, the service is suspended before cancellation. Internal audit closed the recommendation after reviewing the updated policy.
findings.matters: The policy update covers failed direct debit handling and escalation between finance and service teams, which is the sundry debt recovery process a finance director would benchmark against.
findings.quote: 3a. The Debt Management Policy has been updated.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for Internal Audit Q2 Update 2026/27
findings.headline: Trade Waste recommendation 1b, a periodic check of issued invoices against the approved pricing schedule, has not been implemented and now has a revised date of January 2027.
findings.detail: Part 1a, a written invoicing procedure, is complete. Part 1b, the quarterly check, is outstanding; management attributes this to competing priorities. Internal audit has agreed a revised date and will follow it up before the next committee.
findings.matters: Invoice compliance checks on trade waste charges are an income control, and the gap between the procedure and the sampling check is one a finance director at another council could test for in their own fees and charges.
findings.figures: Original due date September 2026; revised date January 2027
findings.quote: The quarterly check has not yet been implemented
